hook_text: Our planet is a giant ball of rock, but from space it looks blue. Why?
clip_script: Cape Agulhas, the tip of Africa. Turn left: the Atlantic Ocean. Turn right: the Indian Ocean. Now zoom out. Further. Further. The Earth is a giant ball of rock, a sphere. But look at the colour: mostly blue! Oceans cover about seven out of ten parts of the surface. The land is seven continents and lots of islands. And wrapped around it all, a layer of air as thin as an apple's skin. Land, water, air: that is our planet.
visual_style: Whiteboard globe spinning slowly, the oceans shaded blue, the continents brown and green, a thin pale ring of air drawn around the edge, then a zoom to the tip of Africa at Cape Agulhas.
mood: Wide-eyed and adventurous, like looking at the whole world for the first time.
pacing: From the shape of the Earth, to its land and water, to the thin blanket of air, with a big reveal about how much of the Earth is ocean.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the seven continents and five oceans on a globe.
